title: Solar and Battery Rebates in Vancouver 2026: Up to $10,000
desc: Vancouver solar and battery rebates for 2026. About 3.41 peak sun hours a day, 15% detached homes. Up to $5,000 for solar and $5,000 for a battery with Peak Saver.
h1: Solar and Battery Rebates in Vancouver
lead: BC Hydro pays up to $5,000 for solar panels and up to $5,000 for a home battery in Vancouver. A battery can keep your lights and fridge on in an outage; the rebate makes it cheaper.
cards_heading: What solar and battery rebates pay in Vancouver
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's solar and battery rebate page on October 3, 2026. The battery rebate is higher if you enroll it in Peak Saver. Every rebate is capped at 50% of what you paid.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW of DC capacity, up to 50% of the installed cost.

cards.title: Battery with Peak Saver
cards.note: $500 per kWh, up to 50% of cost. Enroll in Peak Saver within 14 days of the in-service date. Battery-only allowed.

cards.title: Peak Saver battery reward
cards.note: One-time bill credit for enrolling, then a seasonal reward each winter you stay in.

cards.title: Tesla Powerwall
cards.note: Tesla batteries, inverters and chargers are not eligible for BC Hydro or CleanBC rebates.

sections: Vancouver averaged about 3.41 peak sun hours a day from 2020 to 2024. Summer output is strong; winter output is low. As a rough guide, a 5 kW system here would make about 4,979 kWh a year, using 3.41 sun hours times 365 days and assuming 80% of the panel rating reaches your panel after losses. Your installer's design for your own roof will be more accurate.
More Vancouver households rent than own

The 2021 Census counted 305,335 households in Vancouver, and 166,485 of them rent while 138,850 own. That is about 55% renters. Only 15% of households (44,710) live in a detached house. BC Hydro's solar and battery rebates are for owners of single-family homes, duplexes, townhomes and mobile homes on its grid, so they reach fewer Vancouver households than in the other cities we cover. If you rent, you cannot apply yourself, because only the owner can.
Where Vancouver stands next to Burnaby and Coquitlam

In the same Census table, about 45% of Vancouver households own, against about 60% in Burnaby and about 69% in Coquitlam. If you own a detached house or a townhome in any of the three, the rebate is the same: $1,000 per kW of solar up to $5,000, and a battery rebate that reaches $5,000 with Peak Saver. What differs is how many of your neighbours can claim it, and how much of the building stock is made of condos and apartments, which need a different route.

Vancouver has 18,275 owner households in detached houses built before 1981, the most we cover. Older houses may need electrical panel work before a battery or solar inverter goes in. Get that priced in the first quote. A surprise panel upgrade can change the math more than the rebate does.

A battery stores power for when the grid goes down. The rebate is $500 per kWh, so a 10 kWh battery that cost at least $10,000 can reach $5,000 with Peak Saver. Without Peak Saver, the battery must be paired with solar and the rebate stops at $1,500.
The 50% cap and the order of steps

Every rebate is limited to 50% of the installed cost. You must hire a contractor in the Home Performance Contractor Network and submit a self-generation application to BC Hydro before you install. Wait for technical acceptance. After install, send the final inspection documents and paid invoices. BC Hydro pays within 60 days of approval.
Tesla's Powerwall 2 and 3, Tesla inverters and Tesla chargers are not eligible for BC Hydro or CleanBC rebates. The only exception is an application made before March 12, 2025.
installers_intro: These Vancouver solar installers have the best Google ratings with enough reviews to trust. Ratings and review counts from Google Maps. Ask each one if they are in the Home Performance Contractor Network.
claim_steps: Confirm your home is on BC Hydro's grid.
Hire a Home Performance Contractor Network member.
Submit the self-generation application before you install, and wait for technical acceptance.
Install. Enroll the battery in Peak Saver within 14 days of the in-service date if you want the $5,000 battery rebate.
Send the final inspection documents and paid invoices.
faq: How much sun does Vancouver get?
About 3.41 peak sun hours a day on average from 2020 to 2024, from the Open-Meteo historical archive.
What does Peak Saver ask of my battery?
BC Hydro can draw on it during a few winter peak events, November to March, for up to four hours. You can opt out of events, but opting out of more than half may cost you the seasonal reward.
Can I get the battery rebate without solar?
Yes, but only if you enroll the battery in Peak Saver. Then the battery-only rebate can reach $5,000.
No. Tesla batteries get $0 from BC Hydro and CleanBC.
My landlord owns the building. Can they claim the rebate?

Only an owner can apply, and only for single-family homes, duplexes, townhomes and mobile homes on BC Hydro's grid. Whether a particular building counts depends on its type, so a landlord should check BC Hydro's rules before getting quotes.
Owners of single-family homes, duplexes, townhomes and mobile homes connected to BC Hydro's grid.
